headline: Fed Begins September Meeting as Expectations Shift Toward Another Rate Increase
seoTitle: Fed Begins September 2026 Meeting as Rate-Hike Expectations Rise | FMB Worldwide
seoDescription: The Federal Reserve began its September meeting with economists and major banks increasingly expecting a 25-basis-point rate increase, but no decision has yet been announced.
deck: Persistent inflation and higher energy prices have pushed economists and major banks toward another 25-basis-point increase, but the Federal Reserve’s decision remains pending.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The U.S. Federal Reserve began its two-day September policy meeting with expectations increasingly tilted toward another interest-rate increase.
Morgan Stanley forecast a 25-basis-point increase at the September meeting and another later in the year. A Reuters poll also found a large majority of economists expecting a quarter-point move.
No Federal Reserve decision had been announced as of publication. Forecasts and market pricing are expectations, not an official policy action.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The shift in expectations follows persistent inflation pressure and another surge in global energy prices.
Higher U.S. Treasury yields have also tightened global financial conditions, increasing the cost of borrowing and making dollar assets more attractive to investors.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: U.S. interest rates can influence the peso-dollar exchange rate, foreign capital flows, Philippine bond yields and the room available to the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas when setting domestic policy.
The combination of expensive imported oil and higher U.S. rates is particularly important for the Philippines because it can create both inflation and currency pressure at the same time.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch the Federal Reserve’s formal decision, the accompanying policy statement and guidance from Chair Jerome Powell on whether further increases are likely.
In the Philippines, watch the peso, local bond yields and any response from the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas.

verificationNotes: The article explicitly distinguishes economist and bank forecasts from a Federal Reserve decision.
